survey: A clear crystal ball with a swirl of mist and a pink star inside sits on a gold pedestal stand on a wooden shelf. The camera looks at it almost from the front, slightly above. The stand has a wide stepped round foot that sits flat on the shelf and casts a believable shadow. A narrow waisted stem with a ring collar rises from the foot to a shallow cup. The ball rests in the cup and its lower part sinks into the rim, so it is properly supported. Two curved gold arms rise from the left and right sides of the cup rim to hold the ball's sides, and each ends in a ball knob. The left arm curves out and reaches the ball's outline at about mid-height, sitting at the silhouette edge. The right arm is straighter and shorter, and its knob sits inside the ball's outline, as if that arm were in front of the ball rather than at its side. The mist and star are the usual fantasy content of a crystal ball, not an invented part. The ball is round, the foot and cup are concentric and symmetric, and nothing floats.

errors.where: The two gold holding arms on either side of the ball
errors.what: These two arms should mirror each other but don't. The left arm bows outward and meets the ball at its outer edge near mid-height. The right arm is straighter and lower, and its knob sits inside the ball's outline, in front of the glass. In this almost-front view the arms should match. As drawn they sit at different depths and heights, so only one of them really grips the side of the ball.

fix: Make the two gold arms exact mirror images. Each should rise from opposite sides of the cup rim with the same curve and height and end in matching knobs that touch the ball's left and right edges at the same height, so the ball is cradled evenly from both sides.
